Adjusted EPS of $2.96 grew 9%; GAAP diluted EPS of $2.63 grew 7%, a clean result with no large noteworthy items to bridge (Q1's GAAP figure had absorbed the $425M Greensill charge). The more important below-the-line story is capital return: the firm repurchased $750M of stock in Q2 (4.5M shares), bringing first-half buyback to $1.5B (8.7M shares), and on July 8 the board raised the quarterly dividend 10% to $0.990, a 17th straight annual increase.
Street at: Consensus 2026 adjusted EPS near $10.40; the in-line-to-slightly-better Q2 and reaffirmed guide keep estimates broadly stable, with the H2 margin trajectory the swing factor for whether the year lands at the high or low end.
It also acknowledged the impact of recent earthquakes in Venezuela, where Marsh has 100 colleagues, all reported safe. Assessment: Net immaterial to the numbers, but a reminder that the consulting book carries some geopolitical sensitivity. The slower Middle East quarter is the main identifiable reason for the Q3 consulting deceleration guide, and it is a timing issue against a healthy backlog rather than lost demand. The revenue and EPS framework is unchanged and, if anything, the Q2 acceleration and the raised deployment plan strengthen the case for the top and bottom lines.
